item.title: Conspiracy and fringe-narrative log
item.description:
Not a truth list. Documenting a start date is not endorsing the claim.

Two different problems live on this tab:

  1. Fringe — a conspiracy-style narrative (plot, hidden ingredient, activation, cover-up).
  2. Unsourced — a factual-sounding claim with no solid primary source. It may be ordinary hype, a rumor, or a press sentence that cannot be opened. It is not automatically a conspiracy.

Theories and companies stay elsewhere: [[logs/theories]] · [[logs/companies]].

Fringe narratives

When the narrative takes form Claim Label Notes Pages
2021 era (pandemic microscopy / petition circuit) Licensed COVID vaccines contain graphene oxide Fringe Ingredient lists (FDA, EMA, MHRA, manufacturers) do not include GO. GO used in some lab imaging of spike is not a formulation ingredient. [[topics/fringe/2026-09-16-go-vaccine-5g-claims]] · [[fringe/log]]
Same cluster, viral video GO “self-assembles” or is “activated” by 5G / emergency alerts Fringe Common clip traced by fact-checkers to a pre-COVID high-voltage physics demo (Stanford Complexity Group era), not vaccines. [[topics/fringe/2026-09-16-go-vaccine-5g-claims]] · [[recurrence/log]]
Recurs whenever GO toxicity papers trend “GO is in the water / air / shots because papers exist on GO toxicity” Fringe overlay Nanosafety papers can be real; they do not prove covert deployment. [[weekly/2026-W38]] · [[reference/safety]]

Experimental GO as an animal-model adjuvant is a real research topic. Do not file it as a conspiracy, and do not file it as proof about licensed human vaccines.

item.title: Theories and ideas log
item.description:
Separate from [[logs/companies]] and [[logs/conspiracies]]. Dates are first clear documented appearance of the idea, not “the idea became a product.”

When Idea Status Pages
Late 18th c. Graphite is elemental carbon, not lead Well-supported consensus [[timeline/pre-chemistry]]
1859 Graphite oxidized into a lamellar oxide Well-supported [[timeline/before-1900]]
1947 Single graphite layer as a calculable electron system Well-supported theory [[timeline/1947]]
1960s–80s Strict 2D crystals vs Mermin–Wagner-type talk Often over-simplified in pop history [[timeline/1963-2003]]
1962 / 1986 Oxide-route monolayers; name graphene Well-supported [[timeline/1962]]
2004–2005 Isolated monolayer on insulator + Dirac-fermion transport Well-supported experiment [[timeline/2004]] · [[timeline/2005]]
2007+ Ideal-monolayer property comparisons as product copy Pedagogy vs marketing [[timeline/2007]]
2009+ Copper CVD as a wafer-scale path Well-supported process paper; yield still a problem [[timeline/2009]]
2010s Graphene replaces silicon Largely unmet engineering ideal [[timeline/2011]] · [[timeline/2012]]
2012+ The device is a van der Waals stack, not a lone FET Well-supported research program [[timeline/2012]]
2013+ Flagship-scale coordinated applications Well-supported as a program [[timeline/2013]]
2015 Holey graphene as molecular stencil on gold Well-supported method [[posts/holey-graphene-molecular-stencil]] · [[timeline/2015]]
2017 Shared vocabulary can exist across grades (ISO/TS 80004-13) Terminology standard, not a certificate [[timeline/2017]]
2018 Twist angle as a knob (magic-angle bilayer) Well-supported physics [[timeline/2018]]

item.title: Unsourced
item.description:
Parent tab: [[logs/conspiracies]].

What “Unsourced” means here

The [[guides/evidence-labels|Unverified]] label on a news item: assertion without a solid primary source.

This page is the standing list of those sentences — vendor talk, forecast talk, medical talk, anonymous screenshots — so they have a home that is not “secretly true” and not “automatically a conspiracy.”

Unsourced Fringe
Missing source Story about hidden actors, secret ingredients, remote activation, cover-up
May become Preliminary if a paper or filing appears Stays Fringe until the narrative changes, even if one footnote is real
Often ordinary hype Often recycled as a package

Archive folder for file drops: topics/unverified/ (public repo).
